title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
why_read: A careful ablation study disentangling tokenizer design choices offers concrete, actionable insight for anyone building or tuning language models.
analysis: This paper decomposes tokenizer design into two independent axes, the optimization objective and the search procedure, and builds two new tokenizers to isolate their effects. The key finding is that the search procedure, bottom-up merging versus top-down pruning, matters more than the stated objective for compression-based language modeling performance, at least by the bits-per-byte metric. This is a solid empirical contribution that gives practical guidance for tokenizer construction, though the BLiMP results show no clear signal, tempering the practical takeaway somewhat.
